summary: Arrival Space is a hosted service from Stratum1 GmbH that turns Gaussian splat scans, glTF and USD models, images and video into shareable 3D spaces that open in a web browser, with avatars, voice chat and multiplayer built in. It covers scan-to-place publishing well: splat formats (PLY, SPZ, SOG, LCC), level-of-detail streaming, generated collision, VRM and Mixamo avatars, gates that link spaces, and a JavaScript plugin system on the PlayCanvas engine that is also open to AI agents through a Model Context Protocol server, a command-line tool and a web programming interface. It leaves to others anything about portable identity and credentials, payments between parties, geospatial reference systems, real-world sensing, and published wire formats: it is one proprietary service, not an open specification. Traps for a standards audience: plugin authority checks run only in the sending client, a space export carries links to assets rather than the assets, avatars and inventories move between Arrival spaces but not to other worlds, and 3D Tiles streaming, joints, soft bodies and cross-space inventory exist only as example plugin code rather than as platform features.
